judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard no-conflict representation; the tacked-on stamp duty sentence is slightly loose ('any other statutory duties and levies') but the sense is plain. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the stamp-tax indemnity in Section 4.02(b) but does not contradict it — one is a representation, the other an indemnity. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains the mechanical slip 'would ... reasonably be expect to result', but the intended meaning is obvious and would not change the provision's effect. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses Material Adverse Effect consistently with Section 1.01 and dovetails with the notice covenant in Article III(m). Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional solvency representation using accepted valuation formulations; 'unreasonably small capital' is a term of art rather than a genuine ambiguity. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pairs with Section 2.01(b)(ii)'s fraudulent-conveyance ceiling and the benefit recital, and in an insolvency context those may be pressed together, but they are complementary not contradictory. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One line with a doubled possessive ('all its other present and future senior Indebtedness of the Guarantor') and a forward-looking 'shall at all time' inside a representations article; 'pari passu in right of payment in insolvency' is itself contestable in scope. Modest defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reads as a continuing covenant though introduced by the representations-only preamble in Article III, the same mismatch as (l)–(o). Moderate but minor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains an outright mechanical error — 'none of the or governors or managers' — leaving the class of covered persons uncertain, and 'substantial Equity Interest' and 'near relative' are undefined and vague. Namable defects.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-relies on 'Disclosed Matters', a term defined only in the Credit Agreement via Section 1.01, but nothing in this instrument contradicts it. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It mixes a representation, a forward-looking covenant and an OFAC undertaking in one paragraph, and refers to 'the Facility', a term never defined in this Agreement. Some genuine looseness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The internal cross-reference 'In addition to the requirements of Section 4.13' correctly points at the Patriot Act section, and the covenant tail again clashes with the representations-only preamble of Article III. Moderate-low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sovereign-immunity waiver that mid-sentence switches to immunity 'attributed to the Borrower' in what is otherwise a Guarantor representation — the wrong-party reference muddles the operative waiver. That is a mechanical defect changing sense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Borrower reference is anomalous given Article III's preamble ('the Guarantor hereby represents and warrants'), but no other provision is contradicted. Modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Nine words, using 'Default' as defined in the Credit Agreement; nothing internally ambiguous. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Default in respect of the Guarantor' depends on an externally defined term that is framed around the Borrower, a small importation wrinkle under Section 1.01. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully hedged information representation with an express carve-out for projections; the drafting is standard and self-limiting. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Confidential Information Material' is defined only in the Credit Agreement, but no provision here conflicts with it. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Terms and conditions that are substantially more favorable to the beneficiary thereof' is a comparative standard with no metric, so whether a differently structured guarantee breaches it is genuinely open. The vague term can be named.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a covenant embedded in the representations article and cross-cuts Section 2.01(a)(iii)'s $250,000,000 cap when comparing guarantees given to non-Lender Project Lenders. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The obligation is precise as to timing (five Business Days) and content; only 'would reasonably be expected to result in' a Material Adverse Effect carries the usual softness. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a covenant in a representations-only article and depends on the Material Adverse Effect definition in Section 1.01, but conflicts with nothing. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing proviso — 'the aforesaid restriction shall not apply to an arms length sale or disposal of its assets or properties' — largely swallows the covenant, and 'arms length' is undefined; the sentence is also self-referential ('such Guarantor'). Strong 1.1/1.3 exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A negative covenant that can be escaped by any arm's-length disposal is hard to reconcile with the solvency representation in (e), the pari passu covenant in (f) and the whole premise of a parent guarantee of up to $250,000,000. That is the Lovejoy-style nullification concern.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It repeatedly says 'either Guarantor' and 'either Guarantee Agreement' and refers to 'the Parent' and the 'Unrestricted Account', none of which fits a single-guarantor instrument or is defined here — the text appears carried over from a companion document. The defect is plainly visible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.01 and the preamble define exactly one 'Guarantor' (EGL), so 'either Guarantor' cannot be reconciled with the definitions article, and the provision also imposes a duty on the Borrower inside an article of Guarantor representations. Specific incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical 'except by a written instrument pursuant to Section 4.12' points to the Notices section rather than any amendment or waiver provision, so the only route to an effective waiver is mis-cited. That misdirection changes what the clause permits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against Section 4.12 (Notices) and Section 4.08/4.14 — there is no amendment provision anywhere in this Agreement, so the cross-reference cannot be cured internally. A concrete relational defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable costs and expenses incurred in collecting ... or otherwise enforcing or preserving any rights' is standard fee-shifting language; 'reasonable' is a familiar, workable standard. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It complements the Borrower Obligations definition's inclusion of counsel fees and Section 4.02(c)'s survival clause; no conflict. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow tax indemnity with an enumerated list closed by 'or other taxes', a mild general-versus-specific point but a very familiar one. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside Article III(c)'s representation that no stamp duty remains payable, which is consistent rather than contradictory. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence; the only softness is 'the agreements in this Section', which could be read as the whole of Section 4.02 or only subsections (a)–(b). Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Repayment of the Obligations' uses the Section 1.01 definition that loops through Borrower Obligations, and survival must be squared with Section 2.01(d)'s termination of the guarantee; harmonisation is easy. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear on its face: binding on successors, no assignment without the Facility Agent's prior written consent. Little intrinsic ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.15 covers the same ground but requires the consent of 'the Facility Agent and the Lenders' — two operative provisions state different consent requirements for the same act, a direct conflict. That is a nameable Category 2 defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long but standard bankers' set-off clause; the sweep ('any and all deposits ... in any currency ... contingent or unmatured') is broad but not two-sided in meaning. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It permits the Agent and Lenders to set off while Section 2.07 requires the Guarantor to pay 'without set-off or counterclaim' — directional, not contradictory, but the two are in tension and the trigger 'Event of Default' is defined only in the Credit Agreement. Modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Routine counterparts clause; nothing to construe. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the execution pages, though those are incompletely signed; the clause itself conflicts with nothing. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard severability wording with no ambiguous term. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports rather than contradicts Sections 2.01(b)(ii) and 4.09; no conflict located. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain rule that headings do not affect construction. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bites against the Article III heading ('Representations, Warranties and Covenants') which is the only cure for that article's covenant/representation mismatch, so it slightly aggravates that problem. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It states that 'This Agreement and the other Loan Documents represent the agreement' — a multi-document integration formula whose scope ('subject matter hereof and thereof') is broad but standard. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.14 says this Agreement alone 'constitutes the entire agreement ... and supersedes all prior' understandings, which points the opposite way on whether the other Loan Documents form part of the integrated bargain. A genuine clash between two miscellaneous provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line New York governing law clause with no carve-outs to argue about. Low.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the New York forum provisions in Section 4.10; no conflicting choice-of-law appears. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The permissive 'may be instituted in or (other than by the Guarantor) removed to' leaves it unclear whether New York is exclusive, and the parenthetical restricting removal is awkwardly placed; 'each party hereto submits' also sweeps in the Borrower. Named textual softness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The last sentence of Section 4.10(b) preserves the Lenders' right to sue 'in any other venue where assets of the Guarantor may be found', confirming non-exclusivity while (a) waives forum non conveniens — the two must be harmonised. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It carries an unresolved drafting placeholder — 'a new designee, appointee and agent with offices in [New York]' — and repeated number errors ('the Guarantor agree', 'Each of the Guarantor'). Visible mechanical defects in an operative service clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its closing sentence permitting suit in any venue where assets are found qualifies the New York consent in 4.10(a), and the process agent obligation runs 'so long as the Guarantor has any obligations', which interacts with Section 2.01(d)'s release. Modest.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver is clear, but the final sentence refers to extensions of credit 'TO THE COMPANY', and no 'Company' is defined anywhere in this Agreement — the borrower is 'the Borrower'. A small but real mechanical slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Each of the parties to this Agreement' sweeps in the Borrower and Facility Agent, and the undefined 'Company' must be read against the preamble's defined 'Borrower'; otherwise nothing contradicts it. Low-moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall be effective when received' combined with a permissive list of delivery methods is workable, but the address is fixed only as the one 'set forth below its signature below', which is a self-referential and clumsy formulation. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The execution pages contain one signature block with a blank address and another giving a Mauritius address for a Cayman company, so the notice address the clause points to is uncertain; Section 4.01 also mis-cites this Section as the vehicle for written waivers. Moderate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical '(for itself and not on behalf of any Lender)' is attached to a subject that already includes 'Each Lender', producing an internally odd statement, and 'when appointed hereunder' is loose. Modest mechanical awkwardness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article III(h) expressly builds on 'the requirements of Section 4.13', and the two fit together without contradiction. Low.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The entire agreement of each party with respect to the subject matter hereof' is a standard merger clause, albeit with the odd 'of each party' phrasing. Low-moderate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is duplicative of and in tension with Section 4.08, which treats this Agreement together with the other Loan Documents as the integrated bargain, whereas 4.14 makes this Agreement alone the entire agreement. A specific clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It contains an outright omission — 'the Guarantor shall not the right to assign' — and its final sentence purports to deny rights to 'any Person (other than the Lenders) not a party', a double negative that is hard to apply to the Borrower, who is a party. Both defects are namable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires consent of 'the Facility Agent and the Lenders' where Section 4.03 requires only the Facility Agent's consent for the same act, and its beneficiary limitation cuts against Section 2.01(a)(ii)'s promise of Deficiency funds 'to the Borrower'. Two specific conflicts.
